source.title: DISCOVER: Making Vision Networks Interpretable via Competition and Dissection

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplemental material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares neuron-description results for competitive and conventional vision networks using network-dissection measures, a different method from the audit in the claim. This bears on V4, but it does not audit language-model neuron poles.
record.gate_note: The study tests competitive versus conventional vision networks using neuron-label accuracy and description similarity. It does not test the Qwen3-32B audit, neuron poles, InceptionV1 examples, attribution graphs, or held-out activation prediction. Table 1 classification accuracy is not a neuron-interpretability result. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study changes the activation architecture (stochastic LWTA in place of GELU/ReLU). It then measures the share of classification-layer neurons that CLIP-Dissect labels with the exact correct class (Table 3). That is an architecture-vs-interpretable-share comparison bearing on V4 in vision models. Coverage is narrow: one layer, labels near ceiling on ImageNet Val, no uncertainty reported. Language-model audits, InceptionV1, attribution graphs and held-out activation prediction are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LWTA competitive vision networks keep near-baseline accuracy at high sparsity. They say these networks give highly interpretable neuron descriptions and 'consistently outperform' conventional counterparts on neuron identification on average, by up to 2%. In Table 3 the matched-model average gain is at most 0.3 points. They do not estimate a general share of interpretable neurons.
record.recipe_differences: The study replaces conventional activations with stochastic local winner-takes-all competition in vision networks and applies CLIP-Dissect. It does not use the claimed language-model pole audit or held-out activation-prediction test.
record.method_sensitivity: Neuron-identification results vary with probe dataset and model. Table 2 description-similarity values vary with probe/concept-set choice, text encoder, and similarity method; the paper says CVNs outperform their non-competitive counterpart in the reported comparisons using both text encoders.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 cosine similarity between DeiT-T last-layer neuron descriptions and ground-truth labels is usually higher for DeiT-T/16 than DeiT-T/None. However, CosSimCubed mpnet scores drop on Broden (0.1546 vs 0.1780) and ImageNet Val & Broden (0.1433 vs 0.1821).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Competitive (LWTA) vision transformers yield neuron descriptions somewhat closer to class labels than GELU counterparts, depending on probe set, encoder and similarity function.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-example sparsity: GELU DeiT-T activates ~98% of last-MLP neurons per image (757/768), versus 6.25% for DeiT-T/16. Authors judge the top concepts more relevant for the LWTA models (single qualitative example).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LWTA activations make per-example concept inspection tractable by activating few neurons.

record.problems: The measured exact-label accuracy is limited to the classification layer and four probe datasets, and the study does not establish a general fraction of interpretable neurons. Table 2 uses description-similarity scores rather than a thresholded share. The paper notes that it did not tune hyperparameters for optimal accuracy and that CLIP-Dissect disregards spatial information.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the six Table 3 average values and the Table 2 conditions CIFAR-100 Train with concept set ImageNet and ImageNet Val & Broden with concept set 20k; the latter two each have three method settings and two text-encoder measures (12 values total). Also left out supplemental qualitative examples, which report descriptions but no numeric result. Table 3 averages are omitted in favor of the separate probe-dataset results.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B or language-model neuron-pole audit.
All: no language models, MoE or scale comparisons.
All: no InceptionV1 cat/car or recursive-generalization analysis.

Hidden-layer interpretable share (only the classification layer is scored for exact-label accuracy). Regularization and tool improvements as causes. InceptionV1-sized estimates. Effect of better tools on the share.
All: no attribution graphs or replacement models.
All: no held-out prediction of where neurons fire.

missing.what: Table 3 averages: ResNet-50 76.78%, DeiT-T/None 78.00%, DeiT-T/8 78.05%, DeiT-T/16 78.30%, DeiT-S/2 78.70%, DeiT-S/12 78.65%. Gains over the matched DeiT-T/None are 0.05–0.3 points, though the text says 'up to 2% improvement'.
Table 2 rows for Broden and ImageNet Val & Broden probes with 20k concept set, including the CosSimCubed mpnet drops that contradict 'consistently outperforms'.

record.verdict_notes: Kept as a weak V4 test. The only matched comparison (DeiT-T LWTA vs GELU) shows negligible or mixed changes. The large CIFAR gain is against a cited ResNet-50 that differs in architecture. The labelled measure covers only the classification layer, where ImageNet Val scores sit at ~95% ceiling. No uncertainties are given for Table 3. Table 1 accuracy is not interpretability evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B pole shares and the audit's one-job, two-related-jobs, and not-understood categories.
Language models, dense versus mixture-of-experts comparisons, and scale up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose interpretation, and recursive generalization versus superposition.

The study does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons as in the claim, test InceptionV1-sized models, or isolate architecture, regularization, and tools as causes. It tests neuron-description measures on competitive versus conventional vision networks and uses multiple dissection settings.
Attribution graphs, behavioral explanations, replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict held-out activations.
Automated scoring of explanations by simulating activations on new text, including the share of neurons with good scores.

relation.reason: Its architecture-vs-share comparison in Table 3 bears on V4.

tranche.reason: V4 is about vision classifiers' interpretable share changing with architecture and tools. DISCOVER asks the same question (does an architecture change, LWTA, make vision-network neurons more interpretable?) with a different method (CLIP-Dissect exact-label share). The setting is the one V4 names, not a new one.

source_check.notes: Two Table 3 averages don't match their cells: DeiT-T/16 is 78.30 stated vs 77.25 computed, DeiT-S/2 is 78.70 vs 78.525. So the authors' 'CVNs outperform on average' doesn't hold for DeiT-T/16 when recomputed. The DeiT-T comparison is matched in size, not in training recipe (augmentations differ, Supp. A.1). ResNet-50 comes from [20]. There is no DeiT-S/None in Table 3, and Table 3 shares have no uncertainty.

statements.problem: Minor: 'uncertainty y' refers to the classification-accuracy stds (Table 1). Table 3 shares have no uncertainty. The confound is stated.

statements.correction: DeiT-S LWTA vs cited ResNet-50: CIFAR-100 Train 46.20% -> 55.20% (S/2), 56.10% (S/12). Broden 70.50% -> 68.30% / 68.10%. ImageNet Val 95.00% -> 95.60% (both). ImageNet Val & Broden 95.40% -> 95.00% / 94.80%. So only ImageNet Val and Val & Broden are within ±0.6. DeiT-T numbers as given match Table 3.
statements.problem: After the Broden comparison, 'On the other probes it is within ±0.6 points' also takes in CIFAR-100 Train. There DeiT-S LWTA beats the cited ResNet-50 by 9-10 points. Also, 'matched' DeiT-T means matched in size only: the GELU baseline kept DeiT's augmentations and the LWTA nets were trained without them (Supp. A.1).

The study only states that SoftWPMI beat the other similarity functions, with no share numbers. Table 2 compares SoftWPMI with cubed cosine on DeiT-T/16 as mean cosine similarity, not as a share, so 'untested' holds.
Minor: 'negligible or 1.4-2.2 point drops' leaves out the +1.0 ImageNet Val gain for DeiT-T/8 (T3-11, partial). The overall reading, 'lowers or leaves unchanged', still fits.
For this study only: LWTA DeiT-T lowers the share vs GELU or leaves it unchanged, as stated. The aggregate counts can't be checked from this text.
